confusions: The Questions list is very long and the section headings do not say which questions are under them, so I had to scroll past many screens to find the welfare and housing questions.
The 'Year by year' page's 'Back' button took me to the house prices page instead of the index, so I had to start again from the menu.
On the house prices page the answer was at the top but the first-time buyer age and home ownership by age came after a lot of scrolling and charts, and I nearly gave up.
The word 'Work' on the Work section only showed people aged 16 to 64, so I could not find the 25 to 34 and 18 to 24 figures there and had to go to the 'Did parents have it easier' page.
Words like 'middle-priced home', 'median full-time pay', 'owner occupiers' and 'gross household income' were hard to follow and I did not know what they meant.
'After inflation' and 'Per person' on the welfare chart buttons took me a while to read, and I was not sure which one the big numbers were using.
'Without pensions' was confusing until I read the bullet points below it, and it was not clear from the top of the page what it left out.
The 'Did parents have it easier' answer is one dense paragraph of small numbers and dates, which is hard for me to read and I had to read it twice to pick out the right figures.
There was no clear chart for the share of households who own their home or the state pension age, so I had to work those out from the text.
